title: The Old Bell (poem)
text:
THE OLD BELL

Only a piece of brass, you say,
    A common thing, that's all,
But yet the fondest memories
    Its singing tones recall.

To those whose minds revert again
    To days of long ago,
When some as happy hours were spent
    As they will ever know.

For pleasure they had parties, gay,
    And buggy rides, a few,
All day picnics on river Red,—
    They fought mosquitoes, too.

They didn't have the picture shows,
    Big cars, electric lights,
But youths today cannot eclipse
    Their joys on moonlight nights.

Then, too, the Squintim Dramatic Club
    Was born and did right well,
It raised the money that was used
    To purchase this brass bell.

Some members of the Club are here
    With grandchildren today,
But are they old? No, not in heart,
    They still are young and gay.

—Martha Buford May.
notes: Poem 'The Old Bell' by Martha Buford May celebrating the bell raised by the Squintum Dramatic Club.
